title: Plant-based burger vs. beef burger: nutrition compared

seo.title: Plant burger vs. beef burger: protein, fat and sodium
seo.meta_description: Compare a current Beyond Burger with 90/10 ground beef on the same 100 g basis.
seo.search_intent: Compare plant-based and beef burger nutrition

excerpt: A formulated plant burger can come fairly close to beef in protein but differ sharply in saturated fat and sodium. Normalizing both to 100 g makes the trade-offs clearer.
content_html:
Modern plant burgers are engineered to resemble beef, but the fairest first step is to put both on the same weight basis.

Normalized to 100 g

A current Beyond Burger lists 230 calories, 20 g protein, 14 g fat, 2 g saturated fat and 350 mg sodium per 113 g. Per 100 g that is roughly 204 calories, 17.7 g protein, 12.4 g fat, 1.8 g saturated fat and 310 mg sodium.

USDA raw 90/10 ground beef provides 176 calories, 20 g protein, 10 g fat and 3.9 g saturated fat, with about 66 mg sodium before seasoning.

Protein

Beef leads by only about 2.3 g/100 g.

Saturated fat

The plant burger has less than half in this comparison, although total fat is slightly higher.

Sodium

The packaged plant patty is already salted, while fresh beef begins much lower.

Micronutrients

Beef naturally supplies B12, zinc and heme iron. Plant burgers vary by fortification and can contain some fiber.

faq.question: Is a plant burger lower in calories?
faq.answer: Not necessarily; this one normalizes to ~204 kcal/100 g versus 176 in raw 90/10 beef.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: The beef reference: 20 versus about 17.7 g/100 g.

faq.question: Which has more sodium?
faq.answer: The plant burger in this example.
